posts.cooked:
DerpTheBugbear:

There's been many forms of art throughout history that portray things in an unrealistic manner, yet Comic Book art seems to be one that everyone is okay getting up in arms about. Would you go to a surrealist art gallery and complain to the owner that none of the pieces made sense?  

I believe many object to cheesecake comic art not because of its unreality, but rather the messages that such art conveys. One of those messages is that there are strict physical ideals for males and females, ideals which include overt (and rather impractical) sexuality, especially for women. Some people, myself included, enjoy the unreality of superheroic themes, but don't believe that forced sexuality should be an integral part of super-art.

So no, I wouldn't complain to the owner of surrealist art gallery. But if I visited a gallery of landscapes and every painting included cows mating in the foreground, I wouldn't really want to come back.

posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
DerpTheBugbear:

I hope Adam never changes the way he draws his art for anyone other than himself.  He's his own artist.  There's been many forms of art throughout history that portray things in an unrealistic manner, yet Comic Book art seems to be one that everyone is okay getting up in arms about. Would you go to a surrealist art gallery and complain to the owner that none of the pieces made sense?  

Thing is, Adam's not just drawing for himself. Once you put your art out there on a product, it'll be assessed and critiqued in the context of society, and rightly so. We're the ones paying for it after all, and if we dislike it enough to stop buying the game because of it then we have a right to speak up about it.

And for the record, I don't just complain about comic book art. I complain about similarly harmful imagery in movies, TV, magazines, ads, books, wherever I see it. I fight stereotypes wherever I see them. I'm not picking on comic books and excluding other media.

And I don't agree with the attitude of "it's the artist's vision, let them draw whatever they want". If your work's out in public, you have a responsibility to not perpetuate harmful stereotypes or produce images that contribute towards body confidence problems or similar, in the same way that you have a responsibility to show that there are possible negative consequences to certain behaviours or actions if you're writing a comic book. Far too many artists ignore those responsibilities. If what Adam wants to draw is a scene of sexual assault and put it in a game which is on sale to the public (I'm pretty sure he doesn't) then should we just allow that with no comment at all?

As to the surrealist gallery, I'd certainly provide feedback if the previous exhibition by that painter was in one style and the publicity had lead me to believe that this one would be similar, but turned out to be something completely different. Especially if the original art was refreshing and inclusive and the new stuff harmful.

posts.name: Paptimus
posts.cooked:
Adam's art is referential. Explicitly so. So, even if he plays and distorts some of the codes of the superhero genre, he can't reinvent them from scratch.

Big boobs, second skin costumes, and strapless bras are all staples of the superhero genre graphic code (Wonder woman, who was one of the most progressive feminine hero of her time, has them all). I'm not saying that can't be criticized (it should, and all arguments given here make a lot of sense), but you can't charge Adam of all of this. And I think we should keep in mind that there's also the moral bias always hiding behind such critics, with its own normative values - which are also rightful objects of critics.

There are other biases - with much more deadlier implications - which plague the superhero genre (americanocentrism being the most terrible of all, since it tends to make all non-american humanity become transparent, fading out of the compassion that is requested from the reader). Yet I wouldn't criticize Adam and Christopher for it, since they didn't invent the genre they're referencing to. And they're trying to counterbalance such a bias, in their own way (Haka or Naturalist being examples of that - though there is a lot to criticize here too, if you feel that way).

In the same way, for all the new Miss Information or Mindphyre we get, there are still feminine heroes like Parse, or the Operative in Tactics, or even Becky Blast compared to Glamour in For Profit...

What I mean is : comparing Sentinels' art (or cultural implications) to reality is just due to lead to disapointments. >G didn't create the graphic code they have to rely on to clearly and immediately appear as a "superhero" game. They're not out for photographic realism. Yet, I think they're trying, in their own way, to think out of the mold when they design characters (as much as they can). And you can't blame Adam for getting closer to the code (meaning his art is more easily recognized as valuable superhero art), while not acknowledging how he tries to keep his own distance from it, with some of his designs.

Now if we could get back to the topic and the preorders...

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked:
I think it was around the time Tactics Unity came around that folks started getting frustrated with how some of the women in the SotM universe were being portrayed.  The latex pink definitely isn't my idea of an awesome costume, but I don't want to disregard how much this setting has done for inclusiveness and diversity while trying very hard to avoid tokenism or ignorant pandering (like DC's Bunker complaining that people don't just label him as gay in Teen Titans) .  There are a lot of great characters in Sentinels that aren't straight, white, American men. 

These new designs do seem to fall much more comfortably into the more "male gaze-y" area of superhero design, but I don't want that to turn into critiquing every character for impractical costumes or reality defying design.  Fixating on "realism" is usually a pretty poor route in fantasy stories.  Paul Revere didn't actually complete the ride he's known for in stories.  Chemical plants are more likely to give you cancer than rejuvinate your body.  It's rather absurd and presumptuous of anyone to think that aliens would take time out of their busy schedules of not thinking we are the center of the universe to learn how to speak (mostly) fluent English.  I'm willing to accept that Argent Adept knows how to oil himself up to slip into his costume and Wraith knows the best way to wrap her bandages to avoid any embarassing wardrobe malfunctions.

But it's hogwash to brush off criticisms about these designs due to the fantastical nature of this setting.  "Because comics!" is an argument that makes me cringe because it gives permission for the medium to be written off or infantilized as something that doesn't need a consistent, well-written, and articulate narrative.  I would like to assume there is a reason why a lot of the female characters as of late are busty with form-fitting, reality warping costumes because I trust Greater Than Games.  But people who are fans who love this game and its lore saying that these new designs are disappointing is a reason I totally understand.  Writing that off as a fellow fan or a designer is never a good route, regardless of whether the design shifts or not.
 

For me?  Some of these designs are a little weird and I'm not as excited for them.  It also doesn't help that it's five characters that represent a powerset that used to be held by one character.

See, I like Haka, but if I was learning about Haka and his four other Maori warrior buddies that all had different ways that they were ageless then I may not be as impressed. That's what's so great about the promo cards!  Vernon is my favorite Bunker but I don't need to go through a laundry list of Bunker decks to find the particular flavor of pallet swap ninja Bunker suit I want to play.

Five peeps who are each representative of 1/5th of Spite's power feels like one character for the price of five rather than vice versa.

I hope this works out so that the fans and the creators are cool with each other, because I really like this game and the people it attracts.  I don't know what the right answer is to all of this, but whether the design changes or stays the same I don't know that I'll fall in love with this team of characters who can literally be described as a single unit by pluralizing another character's moniker.  I've been surprised before, but I feel like this is gonna be a hard sell regardless of what happens.

But the cold, hard truth is I'm probably gonna buy the game regardless of what happens with "Jackie D and The Spites" or the quality/quantity of straps on various characters.  I have decks in SotM that have probably only been played once or twice and I'm completely comfortable with a handful of characters in Tactics that I'm not excited by.

I'd sure like to love them all, though.

But hey, at least they didn't go as far as that SotM fan expansion that will remain nameless with a character that literally slings his infected blood at people to make them sick.

That sh*t is disgusting on a number of levels.
